headline: NEW BHP CEO Brandon Craig Signals Open Door for Acquisitions — Biggest Miner Back on the Hunt
snippet: Incoming BHP CEO Brandon Craig said May 13 that the world's largest mining company is open to acquisitions as he lays out his strategic agenda — a potential shift back toward active M&A after the miner's failed Anglo American bid in 2024. Junior and mid-tier operators with quality copper, potash, and iron ore assets are expected to attract renewed scrutiny.

headline: Eagle Nuclear (NUCL) Advances AMERICA'S LARGEST Conventional Uranium Deposit — 27,000-Ft PFS Drill Starts July
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy (NASDAQ: NUCL) detailed May 14 its path to a Pre-Feasibility Study at the Aurora uranium project in Wyoming, which hosts 32.75 million pounds of indicated resources under SK-1300 standards. A 47-hole, 27,000-foot drill program commences in July 2026 with PFS targeted for H2 2027.

headline: BARRICK Authorizes $3B Share Buyback After Q1 Beat — Spinoff IPO of Nevada Assets Targets Year-End
snippet: Barrick Mining approved a $3 billion buyback program May 11 after Q1 gold production of 719,000 oz beat the high end of 640-680k oz guidance, driving a near-tripling of free cash flow. The buyback sets the stage for the planned IPO of North American Barrick, a new entity holding the Nevada JV with Newmont and the Fourmile discovery.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD (TSXV: DRY) Returns 28.8 g/t Gold at Jubilee, Deploys Second Drill Rig at Gold Rock
snippet: Dryden Gold reported May 12 that hole DGR-054 returned 2.92 g/t Au over 14.5 meters including a 28.8 g/t high-grade intercept at the Jubilee Zone on the Elora Gold System in Ontario. The company is deploying a second rig at Gold Rock to expand the high-grade footprint, targeting deeper down-plunge extensions beginning this summer.

headline: URANIUM SPOT HOLDS $86/LB as AI Data Centers Add New Demand Layer — Kazatomprom Forecasts 21M-Lb Deficit by 2030
snippet: Uranium spot held near $86/lb in mid-May, supported by accelerating nuclear power plant orders and surging electricity demand from AI data centres. Kazatomprom, the world's largest producer, projects a cumulative 21-million-pound supply deficit by 2030 as new mine production lags contracted demand.

headline: CHINA'S SULFURIC ACID EXPORT BAN Takes Effect — Chilean SX-EW Copper Output Faces 20% Supply Hit as Acid Price Doubles
snippet: China's total ban on industrial sulfuric acid exports, effective May 1, 2026, is squeezing Chile's copper sector, which relies on acid-intensive SX-EW heap leaching for roughly 20% of its 1.1 million mt annual refined output. Acid prices in Chile doubled from $190/mt to $380/mt in seven weeks as producers scramble for alternatives ahead of peak mining season.

headline: CHINA'S ZHAOJIN MINING Eyes Overseas Gold Acquisitions as Chinese Buyers Re-Enter Global M&A
snippet: Zhaojin Mining, one of China's largest gold producers, is evaluating overseas acquisition targets as global gold M&A reaches its hottest pace since 2023. The move signals renewed appetite from Chinese state-linked miners to build foreign gold exposure at a time when the metal trades near $4,700/oz.

headline: China IMPORTED 790+ Tonnes of Silver in Early 2026 — Solar Demand Draining the Global Inventory Pipeline
snippet: China imported over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, driven by explosive solar panel manufacturing that has made the country the dominant swing buyer for physical metal. Structural industrial demand continues to draw down exchange inventories despite short-term price volatility, supporting a constructive medium-term outlook for silver miners.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Rescues Lithium Demand — Morgan Stanley Forecasts 80,000-Tonne LCE Deficit for 2026
snippet: A boom in grid-scale battery storage is restoring lithium demand after two years of oversupply, with Morgan Stanley forecasting an 80,000 metric ton LCE deficit in 2026 and UBS projecting 22,000 tons. China's power sector reforms drove stronger-than-expected energy storage deployment in H2 2025, setting the stage for a market rebalance that could lift beaten-down producer valuations.
